title: seven WCAG contrast failures shipped, three already 'fixed' by eye
recipe: compute the ratio instead of judging it: parse the tokens, resolve rgba/color-mix over the real surface, check every declared pair in both themes, give each checked surface its own token so CSS and checker cannot drift

problem.symptom: Generated UI carries the tells of a template: colours declared outside the token system, one radius everywhere, emoji standing in for icons.
problem.context: An agent asked to produce a frontend without a design system in front of it.

diagnosis.root_cause: Nothing named the standard, so the model reached for its priors.
diagnosis.why_it_happens: 'Make it look good' is not a specification. A model given no constraints produces the median of its training data, which is exactly the look people recognise as generated.
diagnosis.confirm_with: Run the linter. Each finding names the tell and the line, so it is checkable rather than arguable.

fix.summary: Feed the named findings back into the retry verbatim. 'Make it better' is not a repair instruction; a named tell with a line number is.

steps.why: exit code is the finding count

steps.value: include each finding's name, line and excerpt
steps.why: the specificity is the whole mechanism

applies_when: an agent generated UI and it must match an existing design language
does_not_apply_when: the project has no design system to conform to — the tells encode one house style and imposing it elsewhere is just a different arbitrary taste
the file is a fixture or a test that quotes a tell on purpose
preconditions: a token system exists to conform to
